notes: Extracted 31 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/filterbar.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/filterbar.md (+ filterbar.brief.md) at 3f56271 (the #543 wording fix on docs-next, 29 October), the commit the copy recorded. The guide was written for #164 (Done and live since 28 September, main c1d3642); on main it last changed at 4e470cf (2 October, adopting v0.1.78-3795b4c) and the evidence at cba512f (8 October, the 636f3f5 check). origin/main and origin/docs-next differ only in the Anatomy Field note (“Fully rounded input surface from the public Text Input.” on docs-next) and two evidence Contract lines (and the brief's Field line), so none of them is quoted: the Field part cites the Anatomy description instead. The guide's Sources note says “Checked 2 October 2026” on 0.1.78 (the 3795b4c build); the evidence records checks on 28 September (0.1.60), 1 October (0.1.78 at 5b6894b), 2 October (3795b4c) and 8 October (636f3f5). Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Blobs compared: FilterBar.tsx is 155f6f5 at 5b6894b, 3795b4c, 636f3f5, a116616, c8526ae, ace46ca, dbe0e02 and in node_modules; TextInput.tsx, which the bar wraps, is 17c8f68 at 3795b4c and 2004ac9 from 636f3f5 through dbe0e02 and in node_modules (the field's focus border went from a hard-coded #222 to textInput/border/color at InputState Active, rgb(181, 181, 181); the input got minWidth 0; a name is kept while focused; the wrapper is no longer a tab stop). Its other inputs are unchanged: figma-variables-resolver.ts d03e77c, utils/shadow.ts 1905a41, utils/react-utils.ts bd10632, utils/typography.ts cbabe67; Icon.tsx changed only its loading Skeleton (a81e5fa to 50a809d); the token file changed (0582bb0 at 3795b4c, 4545aec at 636f3f5 and dbe0e02), but the filterBar and textInput tokens resolve the same on both: bar padding 16/10; field padding 14/12, radius 99999, #f5f5f5 fill and 1 px border, 14/18 JioType Var 400 in rgb(36, 38, 43), 18 px icon, so the field is 12 + 18 + 12 = 42 px and the bar 62. So the evidence's 8 October check stands for dbe0e02. Every quoted sentence was read against the installed source: the bar is a full-width column padded by the two filterBar tokens (FilterBar.tsx 83–89) around one Text Input given the bar's modes, the placeholder, value, onChangeText, the label and focus handlers (95–107); focus adds a 1 px #222 box-shadow ring, so the height holds (73–76); the label is accessibilityLabel or “Search filter” (81), and Text Input names its input with it (aria-label on the web), so the placeholder never names a Filter Bar's input; renderInput takes precedence over children, and children are cloned with the modes and focus handlers but get neither value nor onChangeText (112–141); the root is a search landmark with no name (146–155). There is no disabled, error or clear prop; the field's text slot clips, so a long placeholder is cut off; the input has flex 1 and minWidth 0, so the field shrinks with a narrow host while the bar keeps its padding. Left out, and why: the Anatomy Placeholder note's “until they type” (Text Input clears its placeholder as soon as the field is focused, on 3795b4c and dbe0e02 alike, as the Text Input guide says: the human flag); the States Empty caption “The placeholder carries the name.” (it can be read as the accessible name, which is “Search filter”; the Empty state cites the States description instead); In context's “The screen passes the query to its list and shows only matching rows.” as a rule (its “only” describes the guide's own screen; the sentence's first half is the example's from); the Sources sizes sentence (the gap cites the 8 October evidence line instead, which says the same and is newer); the Sources version line; the evidence's 0.1.60 lines (the Rendered and Limits sections, including the 60% placeholder, role="search" and “There is no clear button, disabled state, error state, or result count.”), cited nowhere so the entry carries no stale-evidence flag; the 1 and 2 October #170 lines, which the 8 October check supersedes. Not recorded: style (an override the building rules keep off Coin components), modes and Color Mode, accessibilityHint, the View props, the playground and the Storybook story list. InputState is recorded only as the evidence fact on the field's focus border: no guide sentence asks anyone to set it, so it stays at its default. Strength: one quote holds an absolute word, /accessibility/1 “the placeholder never names the FilterBar input” (everywhere: it describes every bar with its default input; behaviour, so recommended). Nothing is required: no prop is required and no everywhere-absolute instructs. Gaps: #164's comments name one Component Bug, #170 (Done: the label reaches the input and the focus ring no longer grows the bar, re-tested on 3795b4c; “Resting size versus Figma was left unchanged.”); the 42 px field also sat in Text Input's #183 (Done 8 October, the 42 vs 44 px left open “lower priority”). No open ticket covers the 62/64 px bar and 42/44 px field or the hard-coded ring colour. The no-disabled-or-error-state gap quotes the guide's States sentence, so it carries the guide's check (2 October, 3795b4c) like Text Input's and Input Search's entries; it still holds on dbe0e02. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every FilterBar, VStack, ListItem and Text) and no other modes. Example 1 is the guide's In context (TransactionList): a Screen stands for the guide's context frame, with the bar above a VStack of the four transaction rows as Horizontal List Items with the guide's literals; the guide's empty-result Text is left out, since the example's query is empty. Example 2 is the Configuration Prefilled query card (initial “Gold” in the guide source). Consistency with related entries: Text Input's entry (17 October, cba512f) agrees on the fully rounded grey field, the grey focus border, the 42 px field gap and that the screen acts on the reported text; its accessibility rule “otherwise, on the web, the placeholder names the field” does not carry over to a Filter Bar, which always passes a label (“Search filter” unless accessibilityLabel is set), as this entry says; its examples still set Color Mode (written before the building rules). Input Search's entry agrees on the focus border and 42 px field; neither guide names the other, and the Input Search evidence's record of the unpublished MDX (“FilterBar for list-filter chrome”) is not a guide sentence, so this entry gives no when-to-use-which and no useInstead. Leftovers elsewhere: inputsearch.json notes “FilterBar has no entry”; segmentedcontrol.json /avoidWhen/4 “(or a FilterBar, which this pack does not cover)” and its notes “FilterBar has no entry in this pack”. ChipGroup's notes leave out the MDX's claim that FilterBar holds chips; this entry agrees (FilterBar has no chips). The guide names neither Hero Section nor Input Search. Nothing hand-written here uses the shape word Coin doesn't have. Cross-check: round 1 raised 4 flags: /anatomy/3 (Placeholder marked always present; it is not once filled: now required false, and the dropped clause stays out, see the human flag), /configuration/9 (children's “and renderInput is not set” condition lost: fixed), /configuration/7 (value wiring advice the value fact doesn't give: removed), /examples/1 (“Gold” not in the copy); round 2 raised 2: /configuration/8 (children consequence marked discouraged, stronger than the fact: now recommended) and /examples/1 again; round 3 raised 1, /examples/1, dismissed in reviews/filterbar.json (the copy records text, not an input's value; “Gold” is in the guide source). Each round's notes questioned the no-disabled-or-error-state gap's date (answered above), and round 3's notes asked whether “The placeholder carries the name.” is stale (in the human flag). Human flag (reviews/filterbar.json): the builds compared, the “until they type” sentence, the Empty caption and the Focused card's missing field border, for one guide fix (#558, filed by the batch runner).
